summary: Reconstructs POP geometry from DAT tables containing point, primitive, vertex, detail-attribute, group, and dimension data. Its table conventions support a full round trip from POP to DAT back to POP.

key_params.name: createpointprim
key_params.note: Create point primitives when no Primitives DAT is provided

key_params.name: cnvrtallpointcols
key_params.note: Automatically create point attributes from column names

key_params.name: attr0columnstype
key_params.note: Select DAT columns by name or number

key_params.name: primitivesdat
key_params.note: DAT containing primitive definitions and primitive attributes

key_params.name: primtypecol
key_params.note: Column containing point, line, triangle, quad, or linestrip type

key_concepts: Point-table rows become POP points while dedicated tables reconstruct primitives, vertices, details, groups, and dimensions.
Column headers can automatically define POP attribute names and components.
The accepted table structure mirrors POP to DAT output, enabling lossless table-side editing round trips.
P(0), P(1), P(2), Color(3), and array component headers map table columns to typed attributes.
Sequential attribute blocks can override automatic inference for numeric type, array shape, and output scope.
Primitive type values include point, line, triangle, quad, and linestrip.
common_gotchas: The DAT must be structured like POP to DAT output, though the index column is optional for DAT to POP.
Use ? in P(?) to gather P(0), P(1), and P(2) into one float3 P attribute.
Primitive vertex indices must refer to valid rows in the point table.
Automatic column conversion is convenient, but explicit attribute blocks are safer when numeric type or array shape must be preserved.
Provide the matching primitive, vertex, detail, and dimension tables when a full POP round trip is required.
